subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: What Is Friction? The Invisible Brake
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Is Friction? The Invisible Brake.

hook.text: Slide a book across a table and it stops. An invisible force fought it.

buildup.text: Smooth surfaces are rough at the atomic level. Tiny peaks interlock.

discovery.text: Friction equals normal force times a coefficient. More weight, more drag.

twist.text: Contact area doesn't matter. A brick slides the same flat or on edge.

climax.text: Without friction you can't walk, drive, or hold a cup. It's essential.

punchline.text: Friction slows machines but saves lives every second.

quiz.question: Why doesn't friction depend on apparent contact area?
options: Air pressure equalizes force across the surface
True contact happens at tiny peaks — real area depends on load, not shape
Friction comes from air resistance, not surface contact
